en: Mount Pinatubo's 1991 eruption cooled global temperatures because it released sulfur dioxide that reflected sunlight.
The Cagayan River shapes the northern landscape by eroding soil from the Caraballo Mountains and depositing it into the Babuyan Channel.
The Amihan brings cold, dry air from Siberia to the Philippines, causing the cool dry season.
Tubbataha Reef thrives because its protected, shallow waters allow sunlight to reach the symbiotic algae of corals.
The Sierra Madre mountain range absorbs the impact of Pacific typhoons, reducing their wind strength before reaching Luzon.
Tiwi's geothermal power plants generate electricity by using underground magma heat to boil water into spinning steam.
Lake Taal's main lake formed when rainwater and underground springs filled the massive caldera left by ancient eruptions.
The Kuroshio Current brings warm Pacific water to the eastern Philippines, increasing local marine biodiversity and fish catches.
Puerto Princesa Subterranean River formed when slightly acidic rainwater slowly dissolved the underlying limestone rock over millions of years.
The Banaue Rice Terraces prevent soil erosion on steep mountains by carving flat, water-filled steps that hold the dirt.
Mangrove forests in Panguil Bay protect coastlines because their dense, tangled roots absorb wave energy and trap sediments.
The Valley Fault System causes earthquakes in Metro Manila when tectonic stress suddenly releases along the fractured rock.
